owner: HW-05 NoC/Die-to-Die (scale-out topology), co-sign HW-07 Comm-Core and SW-05 Collective
provenance: Chosen by the architecture agent on 2026-10-10 at the user's request, in place of decision point D4 of teams/council/docs/24_TRACE_AND_CHARON_ADOPTION_PLAN.md (the hardware team was to supply 2-3 B-005 candidates). Common scale-out shapes for a 32-rank TP group; pending review by the Collective/RDMA and NoC owners. Replacing or adding a candidate is an edit to this file and a rerun of npm run tau:derivation.
evidence: Every latency below is an ASSUMPTION with a sensitivity range: order-of-magnitude figures for 112G PAM4 SerDes, FEC, cut-through switches and copper cable, none measured on this design. Bandwidths come from the published spec (16 lanes x 112 Gbps per die, p.rdmaDieGB effective, 800 GB/s per card).

card.dieTopologyNote: Die hops between the sending NIC and the die that owns a scale-out port are counted on the 8-die bidirectional ring, the in-card basis of the model (ADR-0016, 2026-10-10: dieCutGB = 2 x uciePortGB, A.dieRing). B-004 is open pending hardware review; the 4x2 mesh of 06 section 3 has the same worst case (4 hops) and is shorter on average.
card.nicDiesNote: The k-th active NIC of a collective (activeNICs = 1 or 3 at the published point) sits on die nicDies[k].
card.portLaneAllocation: Ports take their lanes in order from die 0 upward, 16 lanes per die; a port owns every die its lanes touch.

parameters.meaning: NIC MAC/PCS framing at the two endpoints, once per path.
SerDes TX + RX (PMA, CDR, DSP) of one 112G PAM4 link.
FEC decode per link (every link terminates FEC). 0 = short reach without FEC; 0.12 is about an RS(544,514) KP4 decode.
Cut-through port-to-port latency of one switch traversal, excluding its two links.
Cut-through forwarding through an intermediate card's NIC/router (torus, ring), excluding the die hops between its in-port and out-port.
One die-to-die hop inside the card (A.TECH.ucieHopUs is 0.025). Also rescales the 8 die hops inside cardLocal (collect and redistribute on the in-card ring, 4 hops each way).
Multiplier on the Comm Core control path of each collective class (out/detailed/comm_core_design.json controlPath.classes[].controlUs, O-018).

propagationNote: Signal propagation in copper twinax or fiber, about 5 ns/m; physics, not varied.

topologies.name: Direct full mesh (backplane)
topologies.description: Every card has a direct link to each of the 31 others: 31 ports x 4 lanes = 124 of 128 lanes. One hop, no switch; a NIC reaches the ports on other dies through the in-card die ring.
topologies.risks: 31 ports per card and 496 cables or backplane traces; 4-lane links give 42 GB/s per peer.

topologies.name: Single-level rail switch
topologies.description: Eight switch planes, one per die rail: die k of every card connects its 16 lanes to plane k (32 ports x 16 lanes x 112G, a 51.2T-class switch). Two links and one switch; no die forwarding.
topologies.risks: Eight switch chips per TP group (power, single point of failure per rail); switch latency is on every collective.

topologies.name: Two-level leaf-spine rail switch
topologies.description: Each rail plane built from 4 leaves of 8 cards and 4 spines (non-blocking: 128 lanes down, 4 x 32 lanes up per leaf), for switch radix below 32 x 16 lanes. Up to 4 links and 3 switches; spine chosen by destination.
topologies.risks: Three switch traversals on 24 of 31 peers; spine links may need optics.

topologies.name: 4 x 8 torus
topologies.description: Each card has 4 neighbours (x+, x-, y+, y-, 32 lanes each); dimension-order routing, shortest direction, ties to +. Worst 6 hops with 5 relay cards.
topologies.risks: Relay forwarding breaks the one-hop remote SRAM write; hops x relay latency go straight into tau.

topologies.name: Bidirectional ring of 32 cards
topologies.description: Two ports of 64 lanes (clockwise, counter-clockwise); shortest direction, ties clockwise. Worst 16 hops. The lower bound on wiring, and the topology the ring algorithm assumes.
topologies.risks: Worst-case path of 16 hops; included as the low-wiring reference, not expected to meet tau.

notModelled: 8-card pod with an inter-pod layer (06 section 6 candidate 4): a hybrid of fullMesh and leafSpine; add it here if the hardware team shortlists it.
Optics latency: every link is electrical; a DSP-retimed optical module adds tens of ns per end.
Packet loss, retransmission, link-level replay and congestion control: the model is lossless and credit-based.
MTU segmentation: one message is one packet, as in k3_sram_memory_rdma_model.phase.
